venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Tuesday 7/14 (MOD: MKZ // JK).** Net sales $1,876 vs a $2,145 target (−13%); 60 guests at a $31.27 check average; comps $48.80 (member/investor, industry love, tasting comp, Bingo credit). Food $461; no events. Highs in the mid 80s, very humid with periodic rain early evening, lows in the 70s and cloudy. Steady start to Bingo Tuesday with 12 Meal Deals to open. Guest flow grew despite early rain — lined bar, all booths sat, most of the Mezz filled. Solid food night led by Meal Deals, Jojo's and popcorn. A Bingo guest won four games in a row including the Grand Prize and a Stanley bottle. Flow slowed 8–9pm, picked up with groups at 10pm, then quieted for an easy last call. Opener cut at 8:30pm; stage 5–8pm. Kitchen ticket times solid. Low: banana pudding. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Tuesday 7/14 (MOD: MD; Chef: JMS).** Net sales $1,864 vs a $1,249 target (+49%); 62 guests at a $30.06 check average; comps $56.16 (3%, manager/industry/DNL). Food $274; no events. Hot, partly cloudy with scattered showers. Decent Tuesday, uncharacteristically slow during Bingo — at one point only one group of four playing. Saw two Bingo regulars, one praising the only N/A Margarita they feel confident ordering. A modest pop ~8:45pm was followed by a more sustained push from 10pm to close, mostly first-time guests and industry. John-Michael held down the kitchen and worked the floor during pushes. Maintenance: Well 4 chiller. Low: Patron Silver. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: new regulars from Atlanta returned, this time bringing a new friend.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Tuesday 7/14 (AM: Carey; PM: Maggie H).** Total net sales $9,163.07 vs an $8,082 target (+13%); 123 guests (Tock) at a $74.50 check average; comps $547.55. Splits: DC/AM $1,212.69, D&C PM $7,950.38; food $2,648.50; no events. Bangin', super busy first half in the cafe with Reggie; coffee order placed and light-roast grinder serviced and back up. PM was busy and steady — another solid kitchen night and a busy bar with no cuts; Justin controlled room flow well and servers stayed on top of everything, with Maggie H running IRDs for an hour while Carey kept the floor moving. Kitchen highlights with Chef Lucas, Danté and Marv; a few pops throughout; decent prep tomorrow (low on olives, scallops, fingerlings, burger portions; 911 on basil vin, farce, lamb, carrots, pesto). Maintenance: Lobby men's urinal overflowing (bagged off), Bar 300 rinser sticking and spraying guests. Reminders posted: 2026 Employee Engagement Survey (expires 7/24), bar quizzes due 7/21, Tromba tequila tasting Wed 7/15 at noon in 6A. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Tuesday 7/14 (MOD: Kyler; Chef: Steves).** Net sales $2,656 vs a $4,088 target (−35%); 86 covers at a $31 check average; comps $240 (lots of members, an owner, a few gifts + DNL). Splits: food $209, beverage $2,415; no events beyond the members HH. Hot and humid, first day of a mini heat wave reaching upper-mid 90s. Started with a Shareholder/Member Happy Hour 5–7pm — a decent turnout where everyone had a great time and DK smoozed with the room. Normal service didn't start until ~8:15 but held steady through a short night. Filled by 10pm with a 10-top birthday and lots of other birthdays including a 40th; foot traffic slowed after 11pm. Welcomed World Class 2026 winner Alexis Ortega, Seth from Batemans, and D&C's own Seth. 1 SOF + 1 candle broken. No-shows charged. Maintenance: service well pass.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Tuesday 7/14.** MOD Joe + Chef Vic. Weather: very humid evening — the start of a hot, humid week. Net sales $4,430 against a $4,560 target (food $884). 107 guests at a $92.31 check average. Comps $99 (regulars, industry, an investor, birthdays, DNL). A pretty chill Tuesday, opening with 35 covers. The first couple of hours were quiet but full of familiar faces, giving the team time to knock out cleaning around the shop and some prep. The room filled up around 8pm and a small waitlist started soon after; everyone was seated quickly and the rest of the evening ran smoothly. Around 11pm it slowly cleared, making for an easy last call. Kitchen: smooth night. No incidents; no-shows charged. Entered by Joe. (Report posted 7/15 AM with the date field mis-typed as 7/13 but flagged Tuesday — matched to 7/14 by post time.)

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Tuesday 7/14 (MOD: Josh).** Net sales (incl. events) $3,042.86 vs a $3,286 target (−7%); Marquee bar sales $3,958.34; 72 guests at a ~$42 check average; comps $28.60 (0.93%). Food $594.80; garden closed. Hot. Decent start with a nice mix of reservations and walk-ins in the first few hours; guests enjoyed the experience and the team's hospitality created a welcoming room. Team adapted well to Toast — a few kinks remain but the transition was smooth and workflow improvements were flagged. Business died down around 8pm (cut the opening server), one well closed and a bartender cut by 10pm on light traffic, then a small wave of walk-ins at 11pm before last call. Kitchen had a steady night and sold through all six oyster orders — need to reorder oysters ASAP. Maintenance: Easy servicing both ice machines and PVC piping on 7/16. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Tuesday 7/14 (AM: Braden & Lex/Shannon; PM: James & Marcus).** Total net sales $4,972 vs a $4,000 target (+24%); 128 guests (28 morning + 100 evening, OpenTable) at a ~$38.84 average; comps $313 — majority were voids from an internet outage where guests without cash were comped. Splits: Municipal Bar AM $2,108, PM $2,864, Sun Club $322, Hot Eye $0; food $1,785; no events. Rough electrical storm right before 5pm; dreary night. Good but challenging day: the internet went out just before 5pm at peak volume, so a few payments couldn't be captured before Braden got Toast's store-and-forward card feature enabled; guests were urged to use cash or charge to rooms in the interim. A patient, gracious crowd (many Phish fans staying in the hotel) made it manageable, and servers and bartenders kept cool heads. Sun Club cut short by the afternoon storm. Kitchen: no notes. No incidents; no maintenance needs. Favorite moment: Justin came in and magically fixed the internet.
